answer_1.quote: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities across a wide range of natural language tasks, including question answering (QA), summarization, and reasoning.
answer_1.outputs: reasoning chains with attributed quotes, answers to multi-hop questions

answer_2.quote: We evaluate all methods using two model backends, and DeepSeek-Chat (V3) , to assess performance in different training recipes.

answer_3.quote: motivated by prior studies using LLM-judges to evaluate reasoning , we use GPT-4.1 to evaluate each step of the reasoning chain along four dimensions: (1) its relevance to the original question, (2) its usefulness in deriving the final answer, (3) the correctness of the subanswer, and (4) the completeness of reasoning.

answer_4.quote: We conducted two preliminary clinical reader studies on MedQA , a benchmark based on United States Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE) questions. We first used 593 questions from USMLE Steps 2 and 3 in the official test set and evaluated model performance with ToQ using GPT-4o and DeepSeek-Chat
answer_4.guideline: For each reasoning step, clinicians were asked: (1) whether the subanswer was factually correct (yes|no), and (2) how relevant and useful the step was to the original question and final answer (0-10). They were further asked how logically consistent the entire reasoning chain was (0-10), and were instructed to penalize logical leaps or circular reasoning.
